title: Finding Out The Best All Time College Coach

source.pdf_page_offset_note: Physical pages 1-2 are the MCM Summary Sheet; physical page 3 is printed page 1, so physical page equals printed page plus two thereafter.

notes: All 35 UTF-8 page files were read completely in physical-page order, with Summary, Abstract, and Introduction studied before later chapters.
Visual review used four JPEG contact-sheet proxies of 163936-292171 bytes covering pages 1-7, 8-14, 15-25, and 26-35, plus four formula crops of 106537-135811 bytes for pages 10, 11, 12, and 30.
No original full-page PNG or multi-image result entered model transport; all 35 original 150-DPI PNGs remain on disk as coordinate and fidelity authority.
No blank, clipped, black, overlapping, missing, or failed-render page was found; Table 4 intentionally continues from physical page 16 to 17.
The visually separate baseball coach rows on page 22 confirm that merged names in extracted text are a column-layout artifact rather than source content.

section_map.summary: The two-page summary moves from the coach-selection goal through the AHP-FCE baseline, the classified IAHP-FCE repair, cross-sport and gender applications, a cross-pool winner, time-line plots, four tests, and practical transfer claims.

The abstract compresses baseline construction and 80 percent fit, the two-level repair and claimed 100 percent fit, three-sport and women-coach lists, Pat Summitt, time-horizon behavior, testing, and broader-use claims.
The opening identifies Sports Illustrated and then restates four deliverables: choose coaches, test time horizon, transfer across gender and sport, and write a nontechnical article.
The literature review contrasts peer review, surveys, content analysis, and bibliometrics before selecting AHP and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation as complementary qualitative-quantitative methods.

The assumptions define the candidate pool, Internet-data trust, retained metrics, classification logic, and three first-level concepts, while the notation table binds sample size, weights, judgment matrix, dispersion, CIC, and score.

The data section chooses Internet collection, applies an approximately top-40 screening line per sport, displays sport-specific metric hierarchies, and passes nonnegative metric arrays to normalization.

The baseline model defines benefit, cost, and middle-type membership formulas, a fuzzy matrix, dispersion-driven pairwise judgments, reciprocal consistency conditions, a CIC correction program, and a weighted composite score.

The basketball test builds a 13-by-13 matrix, estimates weights in LINGO, reports CIC 0.032, ranks five coaches, rejects the list against external examples, and turns that failure into requirements for classification and simpler calculation.
The repair groups metrics into first-level classifications, calculates within-group weights, introduces classification weights, and aggregates local scores into the IAHP-FCE final score.
The basketball application fixes Experience, Achievement, and Competency, solves three local matrices, assigns top-level weights 0.35, 0.40, and 0.25, and produces an improved top-five list.
The football application reuses the interface with a sport-specific ten-metric structure, three local matrices, the same top-level weights, and a 76-coach ranking.
The paper falls back to the unclassified model for three baseball metrics and seven women-basketball metrics, producing two more top-five lists and claiming broad sport and gender applicability.
The decision section compares scores produced from different sport-specific metric systems and names Pat Summitt the overall winner before supplying a short biographical justification.
Annual composite-score tables and four coach plots compare gender and sport combinations, then infer bounded fluctuation with a slight upward career trend.
The testing section invokes dimension consistency, top-five membership overlap, assumption reasonableness, and a one-factor baseball rank-stability sweep before declaring the model qualified.
The audience article explains the less-than-ten versus more-than-nine branch, lists sport winners, dramatizes Pat Summitt, and translates the time-horizon claim into advice for coaches.

The final evaluation praises standardization, decomposition, metric quantification, classification, and universality, then identifies indicator burden and missing team-management data and proposes better collection and quantification.
The references identify method, sports, ranking, and sensitivity sources but do not freeze the input datasets, external rankings, spreadsheets, LINGO files, or MATLAB code used in the calculations.

assumptions.summary: Approximately 200 selected coaches are assumed to contain the best coach and to represent leaders of their sports.
The overall winner is assumed to come from basketball, football, baseball, or women's basketball rather than every sport named in the task.
Internet data and all statistical processing are assumed true, reliable, and error-free.
Retained metrics and their classifications are assumed important, reasonable, and sufficient for coaching evaluation.
Abandoned coaching attributes are assumed to have little effect on coaching ability.
Experience, Achievement, and Competency are assumed to proxy coaching skill and team-management ability.
Every metric is treated as nonnegative and classified as benefit, cost, or middle-optimum before scoring.
Across-coach dispersion is assumed to represent the amount of comprehensive-evaluation information and therefore metric importance.
A CIC value no greater than 0.1 is assumed to establish satisfactory judgment-matrix consistency.
Top-level class weights 0.35, 0.40, and 0.25 are imported from unspecified relevant information and reused across applications.
Composite scores from different sport-specific metric systems are assumed directly comparable when selecting one overall coach.
Four selected career series are assumed sufficient to characterize the effect of time horizon across sports and genders.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Internet collection is chosen over face-to-face, telephone, postal, and self-completion methods; sports-reference.com and ncaa.com are named as principal sources.
A screening line selects about 40 better coaches for each sport before Excel tables are constructed.
Basketball uses 13 displayed metrics spanning years, games, records, ratings, polls, playoffs, and championships.
Football and baseball use different displayed metric sets, including bowls and poll fields for football and years, games, wins, losses, percentage, and championships for baseball.
The baseline basketball test uses 39 coaches and 13 metrics, with metrics five through eight treated as cost-oriented.
The improved basketball run retains 39 coaches and partitions 13 metrics into Experience, Achievement, and Competency.
The football run uses 76 coaches and ten metrics, with metrics seven through nine treated as cost-oriented.
The baseball run uses 69 coaches and three benefit metrics.
The women-basketball run uses 15 coaches and seven benefit metrics.
Dean Smith's annual score table covers 1961 through 1996; the prose describes 1961 through 1997, leaving an endpoint mismatch.
Pat Summitt, Joe Paterno, and Bobby Bowden plots are used with Dean Smith to compare gender and sport combinations.
External coach lists are presented as authority or website comparators without archived bytes, retrieval dates, or a unified roster protocol.

models.summary: Select candidate coaches and sport-specific metrics and expose direction classes before scoring.
Convert benefit, cost, and middle-optimum metric values into the fuzzy membership matrix.
Use across-coach dispersion to generate bounded reciprocal pairwise judgments.
Correct a judgment matrix toward reciprocal weighted consistency and return positive normalized weights.
Combine membership values and metric weights into one coach score and rank.
Run the 13-metric baseline on 39 basketball coaches and diagnose ranking and calculation failures.
Partition many metrics into classes, solve local weights, and combine local scores with class weights.
Solve Experience, Achievement, and Competency weights for 39 basketball coaches and report the improved list.
Map ten football metrics into the same three-class interface and rank 76 coaches.
Use the baseline model when metric count is small and rerun it for baseball and women basketball.
Compare reported sport-specific composite scores and select one overall coach.
Calculate annual coach scores, plot four selected careers, and compare gender and sport pairings.
Combine dimensional, list-overlap, assumption, and sensitivity checks into a qualification claim.
Perturb one normalized baseball metric at a time until the ranking changes.
Explain the metric-count branch and publish four top-five lists, an overall winner, and a time-horizon takeaway.

dependency_graph.handoff: Sport-specific arrays and metric directions determine which normalization branch is used.
The fuzzy matrix supplies each metric's across-coach membership series and dispersion.
The dispersion-generated judgment matrix enters the CIC correction program.
Positive normalized weights multiply the fuzzy memberships in the composite score.
The baseline score is run on the 39-coach basketball test and compared with external examples.
Baseline matrix-size, ranking, and calculation failures motivate the classified hierarchy.
The improved hierarchy receives basketball metrics, local matrices, and top-level class weights.
The same classified interface is populated with football metrics and coach records.
Low-dimensional baseball and women-coach cases reuse the baseline weighted fuzzy score.
The basketball list contributes scores to the cross-pool overall comparison.
The football list contributes scores to the cross-pool overall comparison.
Baseball and women-coach lists contribute scores to the cross-pool comparison.
Fixed basketball weights are reused to produce annual score series for selected coaches.
The basketball top five enters the membership-overlap validation table.
The three-metric baseball model supplies weights and memberships for the perturbation sweep.
The paper's qualification claim and rank outputs are translated into the audience article.

verification.summary: The baseline 13-metric matrix is solved with d=0.2 and reported CIC 0.032.
verification.strength: The source exposes a numerical threshold before accepting weights.
verification.limitation: The printed matrix contains suspicious entries and no LINGO model or recomputation file is supplied.

verification.summary: The baseline basketball top five is checked against named counterexamples outside the list.
verification.strength: The paper uses a poor list to motivate redesign rather than hiding it.
verification.limitation: The comparator is informal and the diagnostic does not isolate which formula caused each rank error.

verification.summary: The Experience matrix displays local weights and asserts a satisfactory but numerically blank CIC result.
verification.limitation: The printed expression is only 'min CIC(n)=<0.1', so the claimed value is not auditable.

verification.summary: Achievement and Competency matrices report CIC 0.014 and their local weights.
verification.strength: Both matrices and weights are displayed.
verification.limitation: Top-level weights remain externally asserted and no uncertainty is shown.

verification.summary: The improved basketball top five is compared with a Sports Illustrated list.
verification.strength: All five names appear in both lists.
verification.limitation: Order differs, so 100 percent membership overlap is not 100 percent ranking accuracy.

verification.summary: Football reports CIC 0.051 and a top-five list.
verification.strength: The model interface is exercised on a larger roster.
verification.limitation: External agreement and receiving-sport calibration are not independently measured.

verification.summary: Baseball reports CIC 0.028 and a top-five list.
verification.strength: The paper follows its stated fallback branch.
verification.limitation: Only two of five website names overlap, and the input table is not frozen.

verification.summary: Women basketball reports CIC 0.036 and a top-five list.
verification.limitation: One roster and top-five membership overlap cannot establish gender invariance.

verification.summary: Four annual-score examples are plotted across sport and gender pairings.
verification.strength: The plots expose fluctuation and career-stage variation.
verification.limitation: Selection is called random but no sampling frame, regression, uncertainty, or population test is supplied.

verification.summary: Tables 14 through 17 compare model and website top-five lists.
verification.strength: Membership overlap is visible by sport.
verification.limitation: The metric labels exact-order and unordered overlap identically and calls 100 percent overlap small deviation.

verification.summary: The paper infers that data and assumptions are reasonable from overall model-list overlap.
verification.strength: The intended inference chain is explicit.
verification.limitation: The check is circular because the same assumptions create the scores being used to validate them.

verification.summary: One normalized baseball metric is perturbed in 0.001 steps until rank order changes.
verification.strength: The flowchart states the stopping rule and Table 18 reports intervals.
verification.limitation: Symbols are ambiguous, negative perturbations can exceed feasible ranges, and rank stability does not validate measurements.

verification.summary: The average interval 0.0297 is compared with a 10 percent threshold.
verification.limitation: The 10 percent acceptance threshold is not justified and interval width is mislabeled as model sensitivity.

verification.summary: The Sports Illustrated article explains both metric-count branches and reproduces the key lists.
verification.strength: The audience artifact is connected to the model route.
verification.limitation: It repeats universality and time claims without the analytical caveats required by the evidence.

results_trace.summary: The baseline AHP-FCE ranks Dean Smith first at 0.774 and omits several cited historically prominent coaches.
The improved basketball model ranks Mike Krzyzewski, Dean Smith, John Wooden, Bob Knight, and Roy Williams.
The football model ranks Joe Paterno, John Gagliardi, Bobby Dodd, Eddie Robinson, and Bear Bryant.
The baseball model ranks Gordie Gillespie, Augie Garrido, Chuck Hartman, Gene Stephenson, and Bill Holowaty.
The women-basketball model ranks Pat Summitt, Tara VanDerveer, Nancy Fahey, Amy Ruley, and Jody Conradt.
A cross-pool table names Pat Summitt the best all-time college coach because her reported score is 0.883.
Dean Smith's annual scores fluctuate while the source describes a slight upward career trend.
The Pat Summitt plot is described as more variable but broadly similar to Dean Smith's.
Joe Paterno and Bobby Bowden plots are used to extend the time-horizon claim across and within sports.
Basketball, women basketball, and football each achieve five-of-five top-list membership overlap despite order changes.
Baseball achieves two-of-five membership overlap, reported as 40 percent.
Sensitivity intervals are reported as 0.009 for years, 0.051 for winning, and 0.029 for games, averaging 0.0297.
The public article republishes four sport lists, Pat Summitt, and the slight upward time-horizon narrative.

contributions.summary: Sport-specific metric diagrams make the measurement interface visible before scoring.
Three direction-aware branches acknowledge that benefit, cost, and middle-optimum metrics require different treatment.
Dispersion-driven judgments attempt to replace purely verbal pairwise importance with a data-linked mechanism.
A correction program states an explicit consistency objective rather than relying only on an eigenvalue check.
The paper uses baseline failure to motivate a structural repair instead of presenting only its preferred model.
The hierarchical score exposes the distinction between local metric weights and top-level classification weights.
Basketball, football, baseball, and women-coach applications reveal how the interface changes with metric count and domain.
Annual tables and plots expose the temporal evidence behind the time-horizon narrative.
Four named testing modes organize consistency, overlap, assumptions, and sensitivity checks.
The nontechnical article translates the metric-count branch and weighted-sum logic for a sports audience.

The constraint block and weighted score complete the baseline optimization-to-ranking handoff.
The dense baseline matrix is the main auditable input to the reported metric weights.

The baseline basketball top five exposes the failure that motivates model II.
A generic two-level hierarchy separates classifications from their local metrics.

The continued table and final-score equation show the local-to-global aggregation interface.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary exposes baseline, repair, applications, tests, and audience output, but award status does not prove this sequence caused the result.
The source openly rejects model I and motivates model II, which may improve auditability without proving the revised rankings are valid.
The public article provides a direct decision artifact for the named audience, without proving its universality claims.

weaknesses.summary: Equations 1 and 2 divide by x_max+x_min, so they generally do not map observed extrema to 0 and 1 despite being described as standardization and membership.
Equation 3 excludes x=x_max, has no explicit out-of-range branch, and its denominators do not center the optimum at one under general positive endpoints.
Equation 4 visibly prints an extra 's(i)=' inside the first b_ij branch, and the following b_m definition ends with a dangling 'min'.
Equation 7 visibly minimizes |y_ij-b_ji| rather than |y_ij-b_ij|, so the intended proximity target must be confirmed before implementation.
The printed 13-by-13 matrix contains entries such as 27.42 and visually suspicious reciprocal inconsistencies even though CIC 0.032 is reported.
The Experience consistency result is printed only as 'min CIC(n)=<0.1' without a numeric CIC value.
The paper calls five-of-five name overlap 100 percent accuracy even when the ranking order differs.
Pat Summitt's 0.883, baseball scores, basketball scores, and football scores come from different metric systems and scales, so the cross-sport maximum is not established as comparable.
The time-horizon conclusion generalizes from four selected coach plots without a documented randomization frame, statistical trend model, or uncertainty.
The reasonable-hypothesis test infers data reliability and assumption validity from outputs produced by those same data and assumptions.
The sensitivity equations use r(i,j) for normalized values and r_j for the perturbation magnitude without a clean symbol contract; the sweep can also leave feasible normalized ranges.
No frozen source tables, retrieval snapshots, spreadsheets, LINGO program, MATLAB code, environment lock, or end-to-end reproduction log is supplied.

independent_extensions.summary: Freeze every coach row, field definition, unit, source URL, retrieval time, missingness flag, and candidate-screening decision.
Replace the endpoint-sum formulas with declared min-max, target-distance, or monotone utility functions and test their bounds.
Reconstruct Equation 4 and b_m from a typed specification and verify reciprocity, boundedness, and monotonic response to dispersion.
Compare the printed b_ji CIC objective with a b_ij version and publish the complete LINGO model and solution diagnostics.
Elicit or estimate top-level class weights with documented experts, uncertainty, and sensitivity rather than importing 0.35/0.40/0.25.
Evaluate exact order, rank correlation, top-k overlap, calibration, and held-out predictive relevance as separate validation targets.
Establish measurement invariance or normalize to a common cross-sport utility scale before selecting an overall winner.
Fit hierarchical trend models across a declared coach population and report slope uncertainty, era effects, and survivorship bias.
Use feasible perturbations, unambiguous symbols, multiple outputs, and global or probabilistic sensitivity rather than rank-change thresholds alone.
Ship reproducible data, code, environment, intermediate matrices, assertions, and audit logs with the audience article.
